name: Boerenbridge
description: Boerenbridge ('Farmer's Bridge') is the Dutch adaptation of the international favorite 'Oh Hell!' or 'Nomination Whist'. It is an exact-bidding trick-taking game where players must predict precisely how many tricks they will win in each round. The game is played over a series of deals where hand sizes increase and then decrease ('Up and Down the River'). Known for its strategic depth and the pressure of hitting a zero-trick bid, it is a staple of Dutch social card gaming.

content.text: Boerenbridge ('Farmer's Bridge') is the Dutch adaptation of the international favorite 'Oh Hell!' or 'Nomination Whist'. It is an exact-bidding trick-taking game where players must predict precisely how many tricks they will win in each round. The game is played over a series of deals where hand sizes increase and then decrease ('Up and Down the River'). Known for its strategic depth and the pressure of hitting a zero-trick bid, it is a staple of Dutch social card gaming.

Derived from the British game 'Nomination Whist' which gained popularity in the 1930s. The Dutch variant, Boerenbridge, introduced a structured trump rotation and specific scoring rules that became standardized in Dutch social clubs.
The round number (N) determines the hand size. Start at 1 card, increase by 1 each deal to a maximum (e.g., 10), then decrease back to 1. A trump card is turned after each deal.

items.text: Fixed Trump Rotation: Trump follows a fixed order (Spades, Diamonds, Clubs, Hearts, No Trump) rather than being turned.
